explanation: B combines normalized residual blocks with Adam at a rate that can fit the spiral well within 2048 steps. A’s much smaller learning rate makes learning slower despite its extra depth. comment: B’s normalized residual GELU network and Adam lr .001 provided enough learning speed for the 2048-step spiral task. A used a much slower AdamW rate; C combined diminishing Adagrad updates with stronger coupled decay. K1001, K1002, and K1012 supported this recipe-level comparison without treating nominal displacement as a guaranteed ranking. K1005 helped prioritize the substantial training-rate differences, but its warning remains important: coupled decay can affect converged cross-entropy. This result supplies no new isolated architecture or optimizer rule because the choices change several factors together.
